message.content:
When you toss three fair coins, each coin can land either heads (H) or tails (T).  
With three coins there are \(2^3 = 8\) equally‑likely combinations:

| Combination | Heads count |
|-------------|-------------|
| H H H       | 3           |
| H H T       | 2           |
| H T H       | 2           |
| H T T       | 1           |
| T H H       | 2           |
| T H T       | 1           |
| T T H       | 1           |
| T T T       | 0           |

So the **possible numbers of heads** you can obtain are:

- **0 heads** (all tails)
- **1 head** (exactly one coin shows heads)
- **2 heads** (exactly two coins show heads)
- **3 heads** (all coins show heads)

These are the only outcomes; you cannot get any other number of heads with three coins.
